newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian energy selloff attracts 10 bidders - paper.
newsitem.headline: Latvian energy selloff attracts 10 bidders - paper.

text.p: The sale of Latvian energy supplier Latvenergo attracted expressions of interest from 10 firms, including Germany's Preussen Elektra, Swedish Wattenfall and Finland's Voima, newspaper Diena said on Wednesday.

The cutoff date for the offers was October 15. The newspaper quoted Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA) head Janis Naglis as saying a U.K. firm, British Energy, two U.S. firms and one from France, also said they wanted to take part in the privatisation.
The LPA was not available to confirm the report.
Diena quoted Naglis as saying the bids would be considered from October 21.
He said that an agreement on the sale of a stake would probably be signed by June next year.
The sale of between 25 and 35 percent of Latvenergo is one of the largest since Latvia began its privatisation programme.
The company will probably be made into a holding company with its activities split into various daughter companies.
